articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network Based Image Classification And New Class Detection
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Image Classification is the task of assigning an input image to a label from a set of fixed labels. This is one of the main problems in computer vision that have many practical applications. For any classification problem, the main aim is to achieve better classification accuracy. If the classification accuracy is less, then misclassification happens and this will leads to different kinds of problems. Many of the classification models only consider the existing class instances. When a new class instance arrives the classification model not detect it properly. They actually misclassified the new class instance into an existing class instance. The proposed method therefore shows a better accurate classification and new class detection model for images. Also if needed, then the new class can be added with the model to classify correctly in the future. Recent studies show that Convolutional Neural Network(CNN) can be effectively used for image classification tasks. So here creating this better accurate classification and new class detection model based on CNN. The detection of a new class is done by looking into the trend of the softmax prediction score of class labels. In this work, the model is built for CIFAR10 image dataset. This dataset is actually a complex dataset, so creating a model for this dataset can consider as a base and extended for the classification and new class detection in other images in different applications.

articleTitle: Implementation and Analysis of Flyback converter for active charge equalization in Li-ion battery pack for EVs
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Li-ion battery packs are preferred because of its high power density which perfectly suits in the application of EVs (Electric Vehicles). These Li-ion (Lithium ion) cells in the pack, when charged or discharged will not be in the equal State of Charge (SOC). Also, an overcharged Li-ion cell has a threat of explosion and an undercharged cell loses its power capability. In order to overcome these drawbacks the concept of active charge equalization is implemented with a flyback dc-dc converter, which is designed and implemented in uni-directional and bidirectional topology. Simulation results are validated in MATLAB.

articleTitle: COVID-19 detection from chest X-Ray images using ensemble of CNN models
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The year 2020 will certainly be remembered for the outbreak of COVID-19 pandemic. With the first case being reported in December 2019, the SARSCoV2 virus has proved to be one of the most deadly virus which has affected the human civilization. Relatively high contagious rate and asymptomatic patients also being carrier of the virus makes it more dangerous. The only way to get a control on the outbreak is rapid testing. With the present testing mechanisms being costly and time consuming the end of this pandemic doesn't seems near. These challenges motivates us to come up with a system which can be effective in testing large population size and at the same time be less time consuming. We have proposed a Deep Convotuional Neural Network based ensemble architecture for extracting features from Chest X-Ray images and later classifying them into three categories namely- Community Acquired Pneumonia(CAP), Normal and COVID-19. We have shown that applying such technique can give better performance. Our ensemble network uses three pre-trained DCNN networks namely- NASNet, MobileNet and DenseNet. The low level features extracted from the three DCNN architectures are later concatenated and applied to a classifier for final classification. We have achieved an accuracy of 91.99% which is slightly better than the state of the art performances.

articleTitle: A Rooftop Solar PV Assisted On-Board Enhanced Power Quality Charging System for E-Rickshaw
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: An integration of the possible renewable energy sources with the enhanced power quality onboard charging system; not only increases the reliability of the overall charging process but it also reduces the burden on the grid and optimizes the energy cost per mile. Therefore, a single phase single stage charging system assisted with the rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) of E-Rickshaw, is presented in this work. An isolated bridgeless modified zeta (IBMZ) converter is employed at the supply side as a power factor correction circuit (PFCC); whereas a nonisolated Cuk converter is utilized for extracting maximum power from the vehicle rooftop solar PV panels. The design of the PFCC is carried out in discontinuous inductor current mode (DICM) to ensure the voltage follower mode operation for wide supply and load side dynamics. Whereas, the continuous input and output current feature of the Cuk converter is excellently utilized to extract the ripple free maximum power from the solar PV panel. Furthermore, some crucial benefits from cost, safety, reliability, and efficiency point of view is added in the presented charger configuration. Like, the reduced size of magnetic components, few sensing devices in control implementation, few component count, supply and battery isolation, and continuous charging of vehicle are some features even during the gird outage. Finally, the performance of the charger along with its design and control for a wide variation of supply voltage, loading conditions, and solar irradiation, is verified by using MATLAB Simulink environment. The essential results are provided for the verification of the performance.

articleTitle: ANN Based Fault Detection Scheme for Bearing Condition Monitoring in SRIMs using FFT, DWT and Band-pass Filters
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Heavy duty electrical drives employ slip ring induction motors (SRIMs) owing to their excellent starting and running performance characteristics. However, hazardous working environment prevalent in certain industries renders these SRIMs prone to a number of unwanted anomalies. Therefore, condition monitoring of the working behavior of SRIMs is indispensable for accomplishing substantial production with minimum downtime. In this regard, the present research work proposes an efficient and effective condition monitoring scheme for the detection of ball bearing damage, which is a frequent fault in a SRIM. This is done using stator current as a viable detection parameter. Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and discrete wavelet transform (DWT) is employed for the design and realization of the proposed scheme along with state variable band-pass filters. This forms the three-tier approach for fault detection. Furthermore, artificial neural network (ANN) based pattern recognition is used as a fourth-tier confirmation of the presence or absence of bearing damages as a process of fault pin-pointing. Real-time validation of the aforementioned scheme is carried out in LabVIEW based laboratory interface. Hazardous working environment in certain industries renders the use of sophisticated equipment and machinery to be relatively unviable. Therefore, a simplistic approach is rather indispensible in the current scenario. Therein lays the novelty of the present research work. The entire design, analysis and further testing is carried out in MATLAB/ Simulink and LabVIEW based laboratory interface using a 5.5 kW, 3-phase, 415 V, 50 Hz SRIM.

Author Keywords: fast fourier transform discrete wavelet transform

articleTitle: Touchless controls for passenger elevator
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Control panels play important role in providing interaction with machines. Centuries ago, it started with mechanical switches and has now reached to capacitive touchscreens after a long journey. All these require a contact or touch and in case of capacitive touchscreen it requires some specific type of material through which the contact is made at any point on the touchscreen surface. During the pandemic, the rise of new normal created the need of touchless. Example of passenger elevator can explain the need. Passenger elevators have switches installed outside the elevator cabin, are known as Landing operating panel and inside the elevator cabin are known as COP Cabin operating panel which are touched by lot of people and people are using them fearfully during pandemic. We have developed control panels with which elevators can be operated without the need of touching any surface by fingers and it does not require any special kind of material, stylus or device. Our design is based on Infrared light field which is invisible, low cost and light weight. The design is also easy to install.

articleTitle: A Review of Video Generation Approaches
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Generating videos from some initial frames is an appealing field of research in deep learning. There exists an ever expanding foray of approaches to generate long-range and realistic video frame series. Generating videos can help predict trajectories and even model object movements, to enhance autonomous robots. However, there are only a few comprehensive studies that review various approaches on the basis of their relative advantages, disadvantages, and evolution. Hence, this paper presents a detailed overview of Deep Learning based approaches employed to tackle the complex problem of video generation. The approaches involve Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and even the Transformer model. Finally, the performance of all the approaches are examined and compared on the BAIR Robot Pushing dataset.

articleTitle: Music Genre Classification using Spectrograms
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Music genre recognition (MGR) is an area of research in the broad scope of music information retrieval (MIR) and audio signal processing. Music genres are categorical labels created by humans to determine the style of music. The paper proposes a method to classify music using spectrograms. A spectrogram is the Short Time Fourier Transform (STFT) of an audio signal. They are images showing time and frequency components of an audio signal. In this work, the music signals are first converted to their corresponding spectrograms. These spectrograms are then given as input to the classifier. The classifier used in this work is a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Two CNN models are discussed in this paper: A user-defined CNN model and a pre-trained convnet. Pre-trained convnet makes use of the concepts of fine tuning and transfer learning. The performance of the classifier is evaluated using performance measures such as confusion matrix and classification accuracy. Three music genres such as blues, classical and rock from the GTZAN dataset are selected for experimentation. The classification accuracy is found to be good.

articleTitle: Multivariate Time Series Traffic Forecast with Long Short Term Memory based Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The Intelligent Transportation System (ITS) is one of the key element to build smart cities. For the ITS traffic flow prediction plays a major role for a better traffic monitoring and control, route planning and for travel time estimation. With advent of sensor and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies a vast amount traffic data is now available which helps in performing the traffic prediction. Our proposed work is based on the Deep learning approach for short term traffic flow prediction. The correlation between various traffic parameters such as traffic flow, speed and occupancy are considered for the prediction. We performed the experiment with Recurrent Neural Network based multivariate Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) model. The results show the root mean square error (RMSE) of 9.8 and the mean absolute error (MAE) of 6.6. Thus when compared to the univariate approach the multivariate LSTM technique shows better performance and improves the accuracy of traffic flow prediction.

articleTitle: Optimized Servo Design of SS2 Flex Nozzle Control System for Small Satellite Launch Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Flex Nozzle Control (FNC) system uses Electro Mechanical Actuators (EMAs) to deflect the rocket nozzle for precise steering of a launch vehicle. The servo analysis and linear modeling of the electromechanical actuation based FNC system are carried out to design a compensation scheme based on the closed loop specifications. Friction plays a crucial role in the high accuracy control of the system using the EMA. A frictional model of the system is developed considering both Coulomb friction and Stiction. An estimator based on I-Ching Algorithm is proposed in this paper, to estimate the unknown Coulomb friction in the system. The estimation is formulated as an optimization problem with the objective of finding a parameter value that minimizes the error between the plant and model outputs. A feedforward controller for friction compensation is also proposed in this paper.The closed loop behavior of the system is evaluated using MATLAB/SIMULINK as the simulation tool.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of A Dual Input Hybrid Step up DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Non-isolated DC-DC converters with multi input feature are very popular in the area of hybrid energy integration since they are compact, cost efficient compared to the isolated topologies. A Dual Input Hybrid step up DC-DC converter (DIHDC) with a compact structure is introduced in this paper. DIHDC operates based on the switched inductor technique. DIHDC has two inductors with equal values that are parallelly energized in the initial working modes (i.e., switch on condition) and dissipates the stored energy in series in the final working mode (switch off condition). Also, the proposed converter can be extended up to multiple inputs with slight modifications in the structure. Simple and compact structure, relatively higher efficiency and good voltage conversion ratio are the potential merits of the new converter. Analysis of DIHDC in steady state condition is explained elaborately and the simulation results are presented. A laboratory scale converter prototype has been fabricated to confirm the efficient operation of DIHDC in realistic conditions.

articleTitle: Multiband Hysteresis Current Controller for Three Level BLDC Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: As the transportation sector is promoting electric vehicle technology, the demand for high torque machine is increasing. For high performance the electrical machine drives needs to be operated above 400V DC bus. At high voltage the low inductance property of brushless DC (BLDC) motor can cause high torque ripple which is unsuitable for drive operation. In this paper, a new multiband hysteresis current controller (MHCC) for minimizing the torque ripple in a three level brushless DC motor drive is presented. Hysteresis controller are widely used for their good dynamic response, ease of implementation and overload current protection. Hysteresis current control is well established for two level inverters. In this paper, a three level inverter with MHCC is implemented for improving the current tracking and to reduce the torque ripple. The simulation results thus obtained in MATLAB/Simulink environment is encouraging. In depth analysis to evaluate the performance of the proposed current control strategy is also presented.

articleTitle: Vector Control of Space Vector based Hybrid PWM fed IM Drive with reduced torque ripple
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Voltage Source Inverter (VSI)-fed Induction Motor (IM) produces torque pulsations due to the presence of non sinusoidal voltages. Pulsating torques can be reduced by the pulse width modulation (PWM) technique employed. Special switching patterns applied by division of active and zero vector are implemented in Space-Vector(SV)-based PWM generation to reduce torque ripple. This paper brings up the design of a hybrid PWM fed drive with various combination of active and zero vectors switching to minimize the ripple torque considerably over Conventional SVPWM along with a reduction in ripple current. The simulation using Matlab platform and experimental results with dspace RTI 1103 are presented with a closed-loop controlled 2.2kw three phase IM drive.

articleTitle: Transformer Network for video to text translation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Recently generation of natural language descriptions for videos has created a lot of focus in computer vision and natural language processing research. Video understanding involves detecting scene's visual and temporal elements and reasoning it for description generation.Several real world implementations such as video indexing and retrieval,video to sign language translation etc, are based on this.Because of the complicated nature and diversified content, the captioning problem becomes more challenging.This is a machine translation problem which uses encoder decoder architecture of GRU or LSTM to deal with this kind of problem.But here the decoding starts with the final hidden state of encoder as input.This can't be a good summary of the input sequence,because all the intermediate states of encoder are ignored.This paper proposes a transformer network with deep attention based encoder and decoder to generate the natural language description for video sequence data. This network processes the sequences as a whole and learns relationship between each elements in the sequence by providing attention.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Single phase Bridgeless Buck Rectifier and Single phase Multilevel Buck Rectifier
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper contains a comparative study of single phase bridgeless buck rectifier and single phase multilevel buck rectifier. Buck converters are basically used for low voltage applications. The bridgeless buck rectifier produces more THD than a multilevel topology, also high switching frequencies are used to implement buck rectifier topology. But for a multilevel buck rectifier topology, quite lesser switching frequencies are used for hardware implementations. The multilevel buck rectifier topology does not require a bulky input AC side EMI filter and a bulky DC side inductive filter. From the overall analysis it was observed that the multilevel buck topology has more advantage than the bridgeless buck topology. Closed loop control has been implemented for both the topologies and was evaluated under 24 V single phase AC supply to deliver an output of 20 V DC.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Current Information Based Faulty Phase Detection in Thyristor Controlled Series Compensated Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Identification of fault in Thyristor Controlled Series Compensated (TCSC) compensated transmission system is challenging due to the nonlinear operation of the bidirectional thyristor, and Metal Oxide Varistor (MOV). Protection algorithms which use the current signature based on time or frequency domain analysis malfunction to propagate accurate information about fault condition. It can also happen that nonfaulty phases may detected as a faulty fault due to the replicated unbalance condition in the healthy phases. But such an issue can be resolved by extracting the fault generated components from three phases. In this way identification of accurate faulty phase will be easier. The frequency information in time domain revealed the presence of fault generated components. The same procedure is applied in this work to perform the fault identification task in TCSC line. The Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) incorporated with Teager Energy Operator (TEO) is used to extract and estimate the energy index of the most significant mode. Using the energy index fault identification process is accomplished in TCSC line. Results for different cases are provided which are obtained from the simulation of single and double circuit TCSC line. Both the lines are simulated using EMTDC/PSCAD software.

articleTitle: Analysis of Reverse-Saliency PMSM with Multiple Flux-Barriers for SWPS
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: A reverse-saliency permanent magnet synchronous motor (RS-PMSM) with multiple flux-barriers is presented in this paper. The RS-PMSM produces a positive reluctance torque with flux-intensifying current which thereby reduces the permanent magnet (PM) demagnetization possibility and increases the operating speed range. The presented motor is compared with its conventional counterparts and the electromagnetic performances of both the motors in terms of inductance curves, average-torque contours, torque-ripple profiles, torque-speed characteristics and efficiency maps are obtained by using finite element methods. Meanwhile, the utility of designed motor for applications like solar water pump system (SWPS) is demonstrated. A prototype of the presented motor is also manufactured and the test performances are obtained to verify the effectiveness of developed prototype.

articleTitle: A Novel Comprehensive SOC-Voltage Control Scheme for Lithium-ion Battery Equalization
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel comprehensive state of charge (SOC) and voltage control scheme for battery equalization. For the circuit topology, the equalizers contain balancing circuits based on buck-boost converter topology, which can guarantee bi-directional power flow between battery cells, and each cell is corresponding to one balancing circuit. For the control scheme, real time SOC of each cell is measured to determine the switching state of each balancing circuit so that equalization path can be changed accordingly. Real time voltage is also measured to minimize the load voltage ripple. PI controller is then applied to regulate both SOCs and voltages across the battery cells through the adjustment of the switching duty ratios, thus making a trade-off between equalization speed and battery voltage fluctuations. The circuit topology is constructed in SIMULINK while the control algorithm is implemented in MATLAB. Simulation results of SOC, voltage and current are obtained to validate the control design.

articleTitle: DC Microgrid and its Protection - A Review
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The increase in solar power generation together with the development of electric vehicles and other loads consuming DC has led to the evolution of DC micro grids in the electric power distribution system. However, design of a suitable protection system for a DC microgrid is yet to be fully reviewed. Due to the difference in the nature of fault current in AC and DC systems, conventional AC system based protection schemes and protective devices may not be directly applicable to impart foolproof protection in a DC microgrid. This paper presents an insight into the recent research works that have been carried out in DC microgrid protection by traversing through various protection schemes and protective devices that have been proposed in the literature.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Analysis of Multi-machine Power System with Hybrid Power Flow Controller
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The rise in population and rapid industrial development has directed to large amounts of power consumption, particularly electric power, and to meet the continually expediting power demand, more machinery is being incorporated and, in turn, the stress on the power grid has resulted in stability problems. Several control strategies have been suggested from the concepts of Flexible alternating current transmission systems (FACTS) to improve stability, but these are difficult to implement due to the high cost of the FACTS devices. Unified Power Flow Controller (UPFC) being the utmost flexible of all FACTS Controllers needs to be replaced by an acceptable alternative in order to achieve cost savings along with enhanced transmission system performance. A novel cost-efficient controller called Hybrid Power Flow Controller (HPFC) has been proposed that utilizes previously installed equipment and new Voltage Source Converter (VSC)-based controllers that display similar characteristics to UPFC’s. To show its efficacy in transient stability enhancement on the Simulink platform, simulation experiments with a fault in a multimachine system incorporating proposed HPFC have been carried out and results have been compared with UPFC results.

articleTitle: Wind-Battery-PV Based Microgrid with Discrete Second Order Sequence Filter-Frequency Locked Loop
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper presents a microgrid (MG) system, which includes wind-battery and photovoltaic-array. A doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) is used as a wind power generator (WPG). Peak power from the wind turbine is extracted using tip speed ratio (TSR) algorithm. Reactive power is provided by the rotor side converter (RSC). An improved discrete second order sequence filter-frequency locked loop (DSOSF-FLL) control is used for grid side converter (GSC). It maintains the DC-link voltage as well as regulates the reactive power at the grid. The battery with a bi-directional converter is connected to the common DC-link of the GSC, which is used to store the wind power at light-load condition. A solar PV array is connected at the point of common coupling (PCC). A PV feed-forward term is used to improve the dynamic response of the system. Simulated results demonstrate performance of the MG in different conditions, such as variable speeds within the PPPT (Peak Power Point Tracking) range of the wind turbine, performance of GSC and the battery, RSC and changes in PV array insolation. The grid current total harmonic distortion (According to the IEEE-519 standard, THD is maintained well within 5%).

articleTitle: Harmonic Reduction and Power Factor Improvement of BLDC Motor Drive System Using a Selective Harmonic Elimination PWM Based Controller
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Brushless DC (BLDC) motors offer several advantages over conventional motors such as higher power density, wide range of torque and speed, high torque per watts, high torque to weight ratio, reliability, lower noise and non-requirement of mechanical parts for commutation. They are also being found as an attractive choice in electric vehicular applications. BLDC motors work based on electronic commutation and inherent problems of power electronic circuits like harmonics and switching losses will be significantly affecting the motor performance. In this paper, a control scheme is proposed which aims to reduce the motor current harmonics and their negative effects and also improve the input power factor of the drive system. A DC-DC boost converter with Input Power Factor (IPF) control combined with an Inverter with Selective Harmonic Elimination based PWM and a passive lowpass filter is used to reduce the THD, reduce the harmonic copper loss and improve the overall system performance like torque ripples and input power factor.

articleTitle: A Modified Droop Control Method for DC Microgrid with Improved Voltage Regulation and Current Sharing
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: DC Microgrid is becoming more popular because of its attracting characteristics such as high efficiency, high power quality, reduced cost and controllability. Conversion stages will be greatly reduced in case of DC microgrid as compared to AC microgrid. The conventional droop control algorithms are widely used for managing load current sharing; the functionality of conventional droop is greatly influenced by the circuit parameters such as line resistance. Because of which the output voltage of each converter may not be same, in such condition the load current sharing may get degraded. With the larger droop gain current sharing error can be minimized, but the voltage deviation exceeds the limit, so with the conventional droop always there exists a tradeoff among current sharing performance and voltage regulation. To address the limitations of voltage regulation and power sharing error a modified droop control algorithm is proposed in this paper, which provides equal load current sharing with enhanced voltage regulation. The proposed control algorithm is having a secondary control layer along with the droop controller, secondary layer consists of an average voltage, an average current controller are used at each converter in order to achieve accurate load sharing and improved voltage regulation. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified using MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: A Survey of Bidirectional DC/DC Converters for Battery Storage Applications in Distributed Generation Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: In solar based distributed generation systems bidirectional DC/DC converters (BDC) are inevitable for the control of power flow between storage units and the DC bus. Wide range of voltage gain is the key feature needed for a BDC for such applications. This paper reviews different BDC topologies with switched capacitor technology for attaining wide range of voltage gain and a comparative study is conducted to identify the most advantageous topology. A detailed theoretical analysis is performed on these topologies and the identified features are validated with simulation studies.

articleTitle: Modeling Operation and Simulation of Interconnected DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The aggravation of pollutant gas emissions and global warming has increased the permeance of microgrids in the energy sector. Microgrids incorporate a group of renewable energy resources to supply the load of a localized region and have the capability of both isolated and grid connected operations. They act as a single controllable entity with respect to the utility grid. The main issue with microgrids is the intermittent nature of renewable energy sources, which can be overcome to some extent by Energy Storage Systems (ESSs). However, ESSs cannot be fully relied upon due to issues like high maintenance cost. Hence, besides ESSs, interconnected (energy cooperative) microgrids offer an appealing solution. Whenever a microgrid faces deficiency, it can pull in power from its interconnected neighbor. DC microgrids are more suitable for interconnected operations since there are no synchronization issues in this case. This paper presents the modeling, operation and simulation of interconnected DC microgrids in MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Battery energy support to Cascaded H-Bridge converter fed large scale PV system during unbalanced power generation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: In this paper, a large-scale grid-connected PV system along with a battery energy system is analyzed for unbalanced power generation in the PV system. The system is connected to the medium-voltage grid through a Cascaded H-Bridge converter where each cell of the converter has individual PV and an integrated battery system. With the integrated battery energy system, the intermittent and unequal power generation in the PV modules can be highly smoothed. However, the interphase power unbalance in the converter remains. To inject balanced current in presence of unbalanced power generation in the phase legs, a novel method of fundamental frequency zero-sequence voltage injection (FFZSI) method is proposed. The extent of unbalance that can be tolerated by the converter without going into overmodulation and without sending unbalance power into the grid is established. Simulation results are included to verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Comparison of Passive Damping based LCL Filter Design Methods for Grid-connected Voltage Source Converters
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Distributed generators are typically interfaced to the grid via power electronic converters that are usually operated in pulse width modulation mode. This results in undesirable higher-order harmonics in currents and voltages that deteriorate the power quality. In order to mitigate these harmonics, a filter is usually connected at the output of the converter before it is interfaced to the grid. The most commonly adopted filter is the LCL filter. This paper analyses the performance of different methods proposed in the literature to design passive LCL filters for a 3− ϕ grid-connected voltage source converter. Various filter design techniques are tested for their compliance with the standards IEEE 519-2014 and IEEE 1547-2018. Further, comparison is carried out in terms of essential system metrics such as reactive power requirement, power factor, and the voltage drop across the filter. The performance of various filter design approaches is analyzed using simulation studies on different distributed generator configurations.

articleTitle: Frequency Regulation Scheme Based on Virtual Synchronous Generator for an Isolated Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper proposes a Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) based frequency regulation scheme for an isolated microgrid. The conventional VSG scheme is modified using self frequency recovery control scheme which reduces the frequency deviation occurred in the system due to any power mismatch between the source and the load. The isolated microgrid considered in this paper consists of a solar photo-voltaic (PV) generator connected parallel to HESS with battery and ultra-capacitor. The modified VSG helps voltage source converter (VSC) to mimic the characteristics of a synchronous generator and improves system inertia using hybrid energy storage system (HESS). HESS act as an energy buffer, which ensures faster DC bus voltage regulation. The solar PV generator operates in maximum power point tracking (MPPT) mode using Perturb and Observe (P&O) algorithm. The performance of modified VSG controller was tested using MATLAB/Simulink and compared with conventional controllers under different system inertia parameters with a step load change and solar PV output fluctuating conditions.

articleTitle: Implementation of Five Level Battery Charging Scheme for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The main objective of this paper is to develop a charging scheme for electric vehicles that would be faster, effective, and reliable than the existing system. To do this, we analyzed the battery’s charging behaviors and realized that there is an interrelated relationship between the battery’s current, state of charge (SOC %), internal resistance, and charging time. We noticed that when the SOC% was rising, the battery’s internal resistance was also increasing, and when this value was higher, it opposed the current flow thus resulting longer time to charge the battery. Typical charging schemes use constant current mode to charge the battery. However, this work presents the concept of changing the current values at distinct intervals depending on the battery’s SOC. The proposed work shows the five-level battery charging scheme that would charge the battery swiftly and safely. To validate our idea and design technique, we implemented it into the MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: Conversion of Motor Technology for Economical Solar PV fed Water Pumping System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: With the rise in the use of green technology for energy saving, water pumping has shifted to utilizing renewable power sources like solar energy, for reasons like sustainability, scalability, and an overall clean source of energy. The motors used for these pumps need to be efficient and reliable, to reduce the overall system cost, and to improve reliability. The aim of this paper is to design and improve the performance of a synchronous reluctance motor (SYRM) designed for water pumping application. A synchronous reluctance motor is designed using combined analytical and FE procedure and its performance is compared with an induction motor (IM) and synchronous reluctance motor of the same stator frame dimensions and windings. The comparison is based on output power, output torque, torque ripple and power factor. The obtained results show that there is an increase in output power and torque using the same frame size, and a reduction in rotor material (both copper and magnetic steel), leading to a 3-4% reduction in rotor losses, hence improving net efficiency.

articleTitle: Wind-BES Based Microgrid with Seamless Synchronization
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The non conventional energy generation is a cleaner alternative of greener AC microgrid. This paper presents the performance enhancement of a non conventional energy based microgrid for the seamless grid synchronization. A robust control strategy is used for wind energy conversion system (WECS) and battery energy storage (BES) based nonconventional energy system (NCES) with seamless changeover proficiency from an islanded (IL) mode to the grid-connected (GC) mode and grid reconnected (GR) mode. The NCES has a capability to feed the load both in GC and IL modes and it operates smoothly during mode shifting from IL to GC and GC to IL. The unknown disturbances and ambiguity of NCES in GC mode are taken care by multilayer harmonic decoupling network based quadrature fourth order complex filter (MHDN-QFOCF). The issues like fluctuation in power, DC offset, voltage unbalance, swell/sag produced by WECS, are successfully taken care by MHDN- QFOCF. . With the help of this algorithm, the l quadrature sinusoidal fundamental component (Q-SFC) is extracted. It improves overall system capability of power flow. To control the NCES in an IL mode, the proportional plus resonant (P+R) based control algorithm is used. A dual fourth order complex filter (DFOCF) is combining to phase locked loop (PLL) and develops DFOCF-PLL for precise and smooth synchronization and resynchronization of grid. DFOCF-PLL improves system performance without affecting the stability. During frequency variation, it effectively follows the voltages of the grid and the load and it is adjustable to different conditions of grid. Moreover, total harmonic distortions (THDs) of the load and grid parameters are in the limits of the IEEE-519 standard.

Author Keywords: Power Quality Wind energy conversion system (WECS)

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a Convolutional Neural Network for Handwritten Digit Recognition
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Deep Learning involves learning multiple representation as well as abstraction levels that help make sense of image, audio, or text data. The MNIST dataset of handwritten digit images is frequently used for training, testing, and validating CNN models. This paper focuses on an efficient CNN model with a series of convolutions, ReLU and pooling layers. The model is developed and tested on MNIST data set with 99% accuracy. Further, similar versions of this model are subjected to various parameter variations and the corresponding impact on output parameters are studied.

articleTitle: Permanent Magnet Brushless DC Motor Design for Solar Fed Surface Type Water Pumping
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: An IE4 compatible improved designed permanent magnet brushless DC (PMBLDC) motor is presented here for solar powered surface mounted water pumping. With the growing attention on green energy, focus on solar powered irrigation and domestic water pumping are rapidly increasing. High efficiency, compact size and robustness make the PMBLDC motor highly compatible with the solar powered water pumping applications. Focusing this, a detailed design of PMBLDC motor with cost and efficiency optimization, is presented. This work aims a low cost, high efficient commercial development of permanent magnet brushless DC (PMBLDC) motor keeping the irrigation pumping in prime focus. Considering the maximum usage of the renewable energy and to keep the running cost of the water pumping as low as possible, another aim of this work is to make the developed PMBLDC motor solar power compatible. Initially a mathematical approach for different parameter analysis of designed PMBLDC motor is followed by an analysis validation using RMxprt designing tool. Detailed performance analysis and modelling are done using software made by Ansoft Corp. for finite element analysis. Magnetic material and efficiency of the system are optimized using parametric analysis and FEA tool. For analysis and performance validation of developed motor, an industrial product prototype is fabricated and tested at industrial testing facility.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Single SiC MOSFET Switch Flyback Converter based Control Power Supply for Renewable Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper presents the use of a 1700 V silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFET in a single switch configuration for a high input voltage control power supply (CPS) design in a flyback topology. Such a CPS is used to power the control and monitoring systems employed in renewable power generation, general purpose drives and uninterrupted power supply (UPS). Renewable applications often see DC bus voltages up to 1000 V. Hence, flyback topology is chosen as it provides an efficient DC voltage step-down for a wide input voltage range with low voltage ripple and desirable regulation. The performance of the flyback converter using a CoolSiC™ MOSFET is observed through appropriate simulations and verified through the hardware prototype. Further, the switching and conduction losses of the MOSFET along with system performance parameters are calculated and the results are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Design Optimization of Switched Reluctance Surface Motor using Finite Element Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper presents a procedure for design optimization of 8/6 switched reluctance motor (SRM) using Genetic Algorithm (GA) based random-search optimization. GA is advantageous since it is a highly parallel, randomized and adaptive algorithm with effective global search capability. Selection of dimensions of the motor is based on a constrained multi-objective optimization to achieve the desired performance having higher efficiency with minimum material. Moreover, design of SRM is considered as a highly nonlinear complex problem and is implemented using a 3-dimentional Finite Element Analysis (FEA).

articleTitle: Fragility evaluation of Integer order controller under process and controller parametric uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: PID controller is dominantly used in the industries even today due to the availability of lucid tuning rules and simple structure. There were many analytical tuning rules proposed for stable time delay systems. Very few of them guarantee the robustness and performance of the closed loop system for process parametric uncertainties. It is also proved that PID controller should assure robust performance for perturbations in the controller parameters. It is interesting to note that whether the controller would assure robustness for perturbations in both the process parameters and controller parameters. Hence, the present work investigates the controller fragility for perturbations in both process and controller parameters.

articleTitle: Vibration Data and Analysis of A Large rating Induction Motor with Bent Shaft: Some Aspects
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Operation of many equipment in an energy intensive industry are very critical. The no-provision of standby can increase this criticality multi-fold. The motor under study for this paper is one such equipment where the development of bend in rotor shaft was observed during diagnosis of a breakdown event due to high bearing temperature protection. This is a 1.7 MW Induction Motor of a petrochemical industry. Due to non-availability of spare motor, the motor with developing bentshaft-problem was kept under operation with increased monitoring. The incipient stage detection of the motor vibration due the bent-shaft lead to additional condition monitoring. The vibration data sampled over a period of nearly four and half years with changed bearings is analyzed and reported in this paper. Attempt is made to monitor the defect in the motor with the change in vibration levels as a function time of operation of the motor with the help of vibration trends. Over the period of observation, the average vibrations showed an increasing trend in the range of 0.2 mm/s to 0.6 mm/s with the bent shaft, although these values are well within the acceptable upper limit. Finally, the vibration data is compared with those of replaced (new) motor.

articleTitle: Movie Genre Prediction and Recommendation Using Deep Visual Features from Movie Trailers
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Most of the existing video recommendation models use only the textual contents for recommending interesting videos to users. The textual contents are often missing for videos created by users. Humans are attracted to visual data than any other type of data. Plenty of visual feature information offers people useful inferences. The video classification and recommendation using deep learning is a challenging task. This work proposes a method for movie genre prediction and recommendation using visual features from trailers. This approach segments, each trailer into visual shots of 1 second and extracts the deep visual features of the video frames using the Resnet-152 model. To capture the temporal sequences, it uses the LSTM (Long Short Term Memory) architecture. The output obtained from the Resnet-LSTM model is a vector of the probability distribution of the video segment over the genres (action, comedy, horror, romance). For the recommendation task, this method uses the MovieLens 25M dataset along with the extracted visual features. Finally, the recommendation system will recommend movies based on the genre and rating. This method outperforms current state-of art-approaches.

articleTitle: Position Control of the Induction Motor using Fractional Order Controllers
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel position control method based on fractional calculus theory is proposed for the robust position control of induction motor drive systems. The main aim of the proposed study is to investigate the robustness of the position and speed loops of the direct torque controlled induction motor drive with fractional order proportional-integral and proportional-integral controllers under load disturbances. The torque loop behavior is analyzed through mathematical model of direct torque control of induction motor. The simulation study clearly shows superiority of fractional order PI controller over integer order PI controller. Fractional order controller is implemented in MATLAB simulink with FOMCON toolbox control module.

articleTitle: Grid Fault Resistant Operation of a Grid Interactive PV-BES System with Power Quality Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This work presents a grid interactive photovoltaic (PV) array generation unit, with the PV array (PVA) supplying the power directly at the DC link. The PVA power is maximized by keeping the DC link voltage at the maximum power point of the PVA. The system considers light single phase loads, as well as three phase loads, used in the distribution network, to be the local loads. During grid fault, the control detects the anomaly on the grid side. The system is decoupled and isolated from the utility, and the local loads are energized in an islanded mode. In case PVA power is insufficient, the integrated battery energy system (BES) is utilized. Thus, optimum PVA power utilization and robust supply to the local loads, is realized. After fault clearing, the on-line resynchronization of the system takes place, without disturbance to the local loads. The effect of various dynamic scenarios on the system is minimized, by the fast and continuous estimation of the load current weights, and the rapid update of grid currents, in the event of changing PVA power. Moreover, the grid power quality enhancement is realized by the implemented control strategy.

articleTitle: A Dual-Purpose Multi-Port Converter System for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper presents a Triple Active Bridge (TAB) based multi-port converter system that serves as an on-board charger in one mode, and acts as a power electronic interface for hybrid energy source integration in another mode. The topology employs mechanical relays to shift from one operation mode to another. A photo-voltaic (PV) source, a battery bank, and an ultra-capacitor bank (UCB) are integrated to the DC-bus of electric vehicle (EV) using the proposed system. A boost converter-based Power Factor Correction (PFC) is done to account for the low power factor on the rectifier of the on-board charger. A maximum power point tracking-based slope compensation mechanism is used to integrate the PV unit to the battery bank. The control strategy has been designed to account for the acceleration, constant speed motion, and regenerative deceleration of the EV. All the time domain simulations are carried out in MATLAB/SIMULKINK, and vouch for the satisfactory operation of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Optimization Based Static Distribution State Estimation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Distribution System State Estimation (DSSE) is a popular technique used to estimate the operating states of a distribution system on a feeder basis. This paper presents two DSSE algorithms, the conventional Node Voltage based State Estimation (NVSE) and Branch Current based State Estimation (BCSE) methods, formulated as optimization problems using the WLS estimator. The models are validated on a 33-bus distribution feeder and the convergence of estimated states to true states are analyzed. The performance comparison of the conventional WLS driven NVSE with the BCSE method, is carried out in terms of squared error and average root mean square error (ARMSE) of system state values. Finally, the NVSE optimization problem was solved by varying the number of Phasor Measurement Units (PMU) units installed to study the impact of the number of PMU measurements state estimation performance.

articleTitle: Control of Multiple PV Integrated Parallel Inverters for Microgrid Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: To enhance the accessibility and reliability for a distributed generation system (DGS), a grid-tied photovoltaic (PV) generation system based on multiple parallel connected PV-inverters is developed for microgrid application in this work. This microgrid is designed to operate in the grid tied mode (GTM) as well as a standalone mode (SAM) and vice-versa. Here, a grid-forming inverter (GFI) technology is utilized for system with high penetration of renewables. The single stage PV-battery interfaced GFI inverter in parallel with a PV array supported inverters is considered to operate in the GTM as well as in (SAM) of operation. In SAM, the grid forming inverter maintains constant voltage and frequency across the load The control strategies of each unit are independent and using multi-loop controllers with switching logic. In the GTM, each PV panel in DGS is interfaced with an inverter with independent maximum power point tracking (MPPT) to harvest maximum power. The battery supports the PV units during peak load periods and maintains the power balance in the microgrid. Controlled charging and discharging profile of the battery is achieved by a DC-DC bidirectional converter (DBC). The control strategy of microgrid is verified with simulated results in detail.

Author Keywords: DC-DC bidirectional Converter (DBC) and Power Quality

articleTitle: Control of Solar PV System for Power Quality Improvement in AC Network and Islanded Operation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The harmonics currents drawn by the nonlinear loads distort the point of common coupling (PCC) voltages. It affects the performance of the solar PV system (SPVS) and other sensitive loads, connected at the same PCC. Moreover, it increases the line losses in the AC network. Hence, this paper presents an adaptive filter-based control algorithm for the SPVS to improve the power quality (PQ) in the AC network as par the IEEE standard 519 and to reduce its line losses. The presented adaptive filter algorithm effectively filters out the harmonics from the sensed voltages and currents and reduces the DC offset caused by the sensor circuitry. Moreover, in this paper, an adaptive DC-link control approach is presented to regulate the DC link voltage of the SPVS, which ensures that the modulation index remains less than 1. Hence, the harmonics currents injected by the SPVS at the PCC, are reduced. Moreover, the SPVS separates itself from the AC network to uphold the IEEE std. 1547, if any abnormality occurs in the AC network voltages. In this condition, it feeds power to the loads by changing its mode of operation to the islanded mode. Hence, the energy generated by the SPVS is effectively utilized and its payback period reduces. A Simulation study is carried out in various dynamics conditions to uphold the performance of the presented control algorithm.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Two High Voltage Gain Impedance Network based Boost Converters
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Two impedance-network based boost converters with high boost factor are proposed in this paper. The quasi-Z-network and quasi-Z-network equivalent dc-dc boost converters are modified using L-C-L cell to achieve higher voltage gain. Both the converters have inherent advantages of quasi-Z-source converters which are common ground and lower device voltage stress. The design guidelines for passive components in both converters are established based on the steady-state analysis and operation principle. The proposed converters are also compared with existing high gain converters present in literature. The theoretical analysis of proposed converters is verified through simulation results.

articleTitle: An Onboard Bidirectional Charger for Light Electric Vehicles Using Interleaved ZETA Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The bidirectional power flow operation of an onboard charger (OBC) assists the utilities. It increases the usability of the electric vehicle. In this work, a bidirectional onboard charger is designed and modelled. The design of an onboard charger consists of a voltage source converter and a bidirectional isolated ZETA (BI-ZETA) converter. The VSC limits the THD within the IEC standard 61000-3-2. The BI-ZETA converter controls the charging/discharging operation. The interleaved design of BI-ZETA is achieved to minimize the ripples from the charging/discharging current. The design of controller is such that it controls the transient behaviour of the OBC.

articleTitle: Removal of Speckle Noise from OCT Images for ARMD Diagnosis: An Evaluation of Various Filters
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (ARMD) is a degenerative eye disease among people over the age of 50. This disorder affects the retina and macula of the eye. The macula is the central part of the retina. The function of the macular region is to give a sharp and clear vision. ARMD is mainly identified by the presence of yellow deposits called drusen and the structural changes in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) layer of the retina. If ARMD is not identified at an early stage, it will lead to permanent blindness. The ARMD is mainly diagnosed using Color fundus and Optical coherence tomography (OCT) images of the retina. OCT is an imaging technique that makes use of low-coherence light to capture two-and three-dimensional images from within optical scattering media. OCT images usually are at a micrometer resolution, affected by a noise called speckle noise. If speckle noise is present in an OCT image, diagnosis of ARMD is very difficult, irrespective of whether it is manually or automatically. So, removal of speckle-noise is significant for the accurate diagnosis and early detection of ARMD. In this paper, we evaluate the performance of eight popular image noise reduction filters for its ability to remove speckle noise in terms of different performance measures on a publicly available OCT dataset. Our evaluation shows that, out of the filters selected for assessment, a fast non-local mean filter outperforms all other filters regarding all the performance measures used.

articleTitle: System Dependence Graph based test case generation for Object Oriented Programs
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Software testing is a very important and effort-consuming activity. If the observed behaviour of the software is different from the expected behaviour, we treat this as a failure condition. Failure of a software adversely affects the reputation as well as the monetary status of the development organization. Thus locating faults and fixing it is very important in the development process. Test cases are the input values given to a program in order to find out faults in a program. Testing may be done by static or dynamic method. In static testing, the target code is not executed, whereas in dynamic method, the target code is executed. A major static testing method is the code review, in which the syntax and usage of various elements of the code are reviewed. The goal of this work is to generate test cases to statically validate the array index so that the unexpected array index boundary violations can be tested. For this the Java source code is analysed using SDG and the proposed tool is implemented using Antlr with Java grammar by embedding action codes in the grammar.

articleTitle: Bridging the Broadband Gap and Power Up To 5G
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: As the commercial wireless communication technology evolves from 4G to 5G, it'll boost the demand for data rate and spectrum efficiency. Doherty power amplifiers (DPAs), one of the foremost widely used power amplifiers (PAs) within the cellular communication systems, had received extensive attention in modern research thanks to its higher efficiency across an out-sized power range and featured simplicity within the circuit implementation. Several researchers proved that it could operate in mm-wave frequency. Unfortunately, it's some intrinsic bandwidth (BW) limitations. BW extension of DPA plays a significant step in modern 5G PA designs. This paper briefly reviews PA evolution techniques, envelope tracking (ET) PAs, DPAs, reasons for DPA BW limitations, BW extension techniques followed by major challenges headed by BW extended DPAs shortly.

articleTitle: The Untapped Potential of Feature Selection for Emotion Recognition: Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Emotional state identification has many applications in human computer interaction, intelligent machine interface, smart classrooms and medical application. Many approaches are introduced to recognize emotions from face expression, speech, gesture, body poses and skin conductance. There is a high correlation between emotions and physiological changes and since they are unconscious responses, physiological signals have added benefits. Electrocardiogram (ECG) is one of the physiological signals, which results from activity of autonomous nervous system (ANS) reflects the underlying true emotional state. The aim of this work is to give an overview of methods to select features from ECG contributing to emotion recognition. The reviewed studies reveal that the best combination of features leads to improved accuracy.

articleTitle: Control of Wind-Battery Based Microgrid With Seamless Synchronization to Grid/DG Set
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper deals with the control of wind turbine driven induction generator-battery based microgrid with seamless synchronization to the grid/DG-set. Here, two voltage source converters (machine side converter and load side converter) are used to connect the wind generator, household loads and the grid with each other. The machine side converter (MSC) is controlled using the sensorless field-oriented vector control to eliminate the mechanical sensor. The load side converter (LSC) is controlled with an adaptive algorithm and operates the microgrid in off-grid mode, grid connected mode and DG-set connected mode. The microgrid control strategies are tested on MATLAB/Simulink and on hardware prototype under various operating conditions such load unbalance, wind speed variation and during grid/DG set synchronization

articleTitle: Fundamental Frequency Switched VSC with PV-STATCOM Feature for Large-Scale Solar PV Plant
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: In this paper, a new configuration of a 24-pulse voltage source converter (VSC) based on three-level neutral point clamp converter (NPC) and multi-winding transformer (MWT) is proposed for large-scale solar photovoltaic (PV) plant. Fundamental frequency switching (FFS) modulation is used for gating pulses generation. This FFS modulated NPC-MWT based 24-pulse VSC has low voltage and current harmonics, low switching losses, and allows direct high voltage (HV) grid integration. Additionally, it is used as PV-STATCOM for providing necessary reactive power support to the grid during the day and nighttime for grid voltage regulation. In Matlab environment a model of a 5MW NPC-MWT based 24-pulse three-level VSC is built to validate the design and control. Harmonics, steady-state and dynamic performances of it, are demonstrated in detail to validate the proposed concept.

articleTitle: Futuristic Model of Automatic Electric Cooking Machine
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Automation is taking place in almost all the fields. The aim of this project is to make an innovation in the kitchen. This new design of automated electric cooker can work on IOT platform. For operating the project on IOT platform Blynk application and NodeMCU ESP8266 is used. An induction coil is placed at one side of the pan. For inductive heating a Quasi-Resonant converter is used. In order to reach heat in all sides of the Pan and to mix the ingredients, it must be rotated and tilted at a particular angle. For rotating the cooker at a particular speed, BLDC motor is used. The speed of the BLDC motor is adjusted based on the temperature of pan in-order to avoid sticking of food materials. The cooker is tilted using a servo motor. The food ingredients are placed on the pot using a robotic arm.

articleTitle: Identification of shockwave and muzzle blast in a gunshot signal using frequency analysis techniques
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The development of an acoustic sensor system used for locating the source of the firing of a weapon is highly challenging. The main challenge is identifying shockwave (SW) and muzzle blast (MB) from the fired signal and computing their arrival time. Incorrect identification of these signals will lead to a false location of the source. This paper discusses three joint time-frequency analysis techniques to identify the shock wave and muzzle blast in a gunshot signal. Techniques include Short Time Fourier Transform (STFT), Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT), and Synchro Squeezing Transform (SST). Gunshot signals fired from various weapons at different positions were analyzed using these techniques.

articleTitle: Design of Inner-Rotor PMBLDC Motor for Water Pumping
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper deals with a simplified analytical procedure for designing surface mounted permanent magnet brushless DC (PMBLDC) motor for water pumping application. Analytical techniques provide preliminary machine design and require lesser time compared to computationally intensive finite element analysis (FEA) techniques. Design steps are scripted in MATLAB environment to design 6-pole 3-hp, 2500 RPM fully enclosed inner rotor type PMBLDC motor. Results obtained from analytical technique are refined and analysed using MotorXP analysis software. Effectiveness of design methodology is verified by comparing the performance parameters like required output power, torque, efficiency and flux density with required rated data.

articleTitle: A Home Charging System for EVs Using Vienna Based Modified Cuk Converter and LLC Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper presents home charging system for e-rickshaw with two stage power conversion. The charging system has AC-DC and DC-DC power conversion stage with an isolation transformer. The AC-DC power conversion is made by modified Cuk converter based on Vienna rectification, which is used to maintain power quality according to IEC 61000-3-2 international standard and to maintain constant DC-link with the variation in AC power supply. The output of primary stage is fed to split DC-link. The second stage has half bridge isolated converter with passive rectification on secondary side. This DC-DC power stage is used to control the charging of battery of EV, the charging control is made through frequency modulation. The change in switching frequency changes the power transfer with the variation in effective value in transfer inductance. In order to determine performance of front end converter, the state space model is developed and its frequency response Bode plot is determined with designed parameters under both open and closed loop conditions. For this, a 1.5 kW EV charging system is designed and simulated on MATLAB/Simulink and simulation results at different input and output conditions show the effectiveness of charging system.

articleTitle: A Modified CNN for Detection of Faults During Power Swing in Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Fault detection, classification, and identification of location are key to ensure normal operation and healthiness of the power system including extra high voltage (EHV) and ultra-high voltage (UHV) transmission lines, where almost 85% of faults occur. One of the most important feature in distance relays is the power swing blocking function, a key element for preventing unintended tripping of transmission lines. Distinction of faults from power swing should be quick and specific to reduce widespread blackouts, and economic losses. This lead to the introduction of newer methods on fault analysis for much faster and accurate operation of relays. Modern methods use machine learning techniques which are still at its early stage. This paper proposes a modified 1-D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture to identify power swings and fault cases with high accuracy. An infinite bus system and Western System Coordinating Council (WSCC) 3-machine, 9-bus system are selected for investigating different fault conditions during power swing. A comparative analysis of different traditional machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques are also conducted to validate the efficacy of proposed methodology.

articleTitle: Investigation of PLLs for Distributed Generation Systems in the Grid-connected Mode of Operation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The distributed generation systems (DGs) include the phase-locked loop (PLL) controller when incorporated into the grid for synchronization. In this paper, we presented the three foremost PLL based grid synchronization methods, and the examination of PLLs for parallel-connected DGs when they integrated into the grid is introduced. Specifically, the exhibition of the PLLs under different conditions is investigated. The PLL strategy for grid-integrated parallel-connected multiple DGs is implemented in Typhoon hardware in the loop software platform and verified with Typhoon 402 hardware equipment. The outcomes obviously show the viability of the examined PLL controllers in grid-integrated operation for the multiple parallel-connected DGs.

articleTitle: A Three-Level NPC Fed Induction Motor Drive With Closed Loop DC-Link Voltage Balancing Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper presents a closed loop space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) based dc bus voltage balancing algorithm for a three-level neutral-point-clamped (3L-NPC) inverter fed induction motor drive. Broad range of accurate speed and torque control is achieved using rotor field-oriented control (RFOC). Switching sequences for the NPC inverter are designed based on the degree of dc-link voltage unbalance and dc-link current to achieve dc-link capacitor voltage balancing under various load conditions. The algorithm is effective for both motoring and regenerative braking modes, which is the most adequate requirement for electric vehicle application. The redundant switching states in small voltage space vectors are utilized to enhance the harmonic performance of the inverter and capacitor voltage balancing. Performance of the 3L-NPC fed induction motor drive is studied in MATLAB/SIMULINK platform.

articleTitle: Robust Scheduling of Electric Vehicle Charging for PV Integrated Parking-lots
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper proposes a robust charging scheduling scheme for Electric Vehicle (EV) in a commercial PV integrated parking lot. There are uncertainties in information of parking lot EV charging management problem, like arrival and departure time of EVs, PV power generation and cost of electricity. An event triggered approach can tackle the charging demand uncertainty of EVs. For PV power generation, a short term forecast model based on XGBoost algorithm is used for mitigating renewable energy uncertainty. Finally a real time EV charging scheduling problem is developed that can minimize the operating cost of the parking lot operator at the same time the charging demands of all the connected EVs are satisfied. From the simulation results we can infer that the proposed algorithm guarantees the stability and robustness of system uncertainties in particular, irregular EV arrival and departure and power generation from PV system.

articleTitle: Scalable Generic Platform For Big Data Visualization
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The term data analytics is referred to as the study of raw data to gain knowledge. Visualizations are the best way to represent the analyzed data so that it could be consumed by anyone on the go. However, when the amount of data increases and use cases differ, creating these visualizations indulge difficulties and will become repetitive yet hectic tasks. The insights platform depicted here is a generic platform to ease the above said complex process. Here, a generalized platform is made using the internal data from the company and a full stack application is furnished. Since it's developed keeping the generic aspect in mind, the platform could be used for a wide range of use cases by making changes to the data engineering configurations and visualization queries. All others will remain the same and hence new and new applications could be developed in no time with much ease.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Path Control Strategies for Unmanned Quadrotor Aerial Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Due to highly coupled nonlinear dynamics with underactuated nature, designing controllers for quadrotor is a hard job. This paper presents a comparative analysis of proportional integral derivative, linear quadratic regulator and model predictive controller as path controllers for unmanned quadrotor aircraft. MATLAB/Simulink based simulation studies shows that model predictive control can handle multi-input multi-output system by considering future task references.

articleTitle: Route Request Flooding based Denial of Service Attack in Wireless Ad Hoc Networks and Selected Defending Measures: A Review
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Wireless Ad Hoc Networks are gaining popularity nowadays due to easiness in deployment and management of the network. They are self organizing wireless networks formed by mobile nodes on-the-fly without using any fixed infrastructure. They are widely useful in military based applications, emergency search and rescue operation during disaster management or even communication in big superstores. However, due to their decentralized and distributed operation, security is a major concern in these type of networks. Limited computational capability of the nodes and lower battery backup created added constraints which further reduces the possibility of using cryptographic techniques in securing these networks. Availability is one of the security requirements needed for any wireless networks. Threat to availability is Denial of Service (DoS) attack. Flooding attack is one of various DoS attacks that can be launched from various layer of protocol stack. This paper is intended to provide a review of Route Request (RREQ) flooding attack and their state-of-the-art remedial measures in Wireless Ad Hoc Networks.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Control Strategy for Remotely Located Microgrid Comprised of Solar PV-Battery Storage-Synchronous Generator Based DG Set
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: In this paper, a modified leaky-least mean square (MLLMS) control strategy for remotely located microgrid includes solar photovoltaic (PV), battery storage (BS) and diesel generator (DG) set is developed to provide continuous supply to remote locations. The storage battery is integrated at the DC link with the help of a bidirectional buck-boost converter (BDC). It functions as a buck converter during the charging of the battery. Whereas it operates as a boost converter when it discharges power. Moreover, the BDC fixes PV maximum power point (MPP) voltage at the DC link; thereby, peak power is harvested. Here, a synchronous generator based DG set is connected at the point of common interphase (PCI) to provide the load demand. It feeds linear or nonlinear loads. The linear and nonlinear loads demand reactive power and harmonics; thus, the voltage source converter (VSC) that integrates the energy sources at the PCI is controlled to compensate for power quality (PQ) issues.

articleTitle: Classification of Motor Imagery Signals Using ANFIS to Control a Robotic System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) aims to provide a communication between the brain and the computer for the benefit of disabled people. The Motor cortex is the region of the cerebral cortex involved in the planning and control of voluntary movements. The motor imagery signal corresponding to an imagined action, EEG signal (Electro Encephalogram), is obtained from the motor cortex. EEG is a non-stationary signal with a low signal to noise ratio. Moreover, subject dependent variability, the requirement of optimum feature extraction methods and, demand for highly accurate classifier is still the major challenges in Motor Imagery based BCI.
