Several works were reported in BCI, but in this work, we propose a method to overcome the above issues to a considerable extent. The proposed method uses the Common Spatial Pattern (CSP) algorithm with Joint Approximate Diagonalization (JAD) to extract optimum features. Classification is carried out using an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS). The proposed method is trained and tested using a publically available BCI competition IV data set. The result obtained in this approach is found to be far better than many other reported results. The four imagined movements Left- hand movement (class 1), Right-hand movement (class 2), Foot movement (class 3) and, the Tongue movement (class 4) were demonstrated using a robotic system. Lego Mind-storm NXT brick controller is used to control the robotic structure. The four classified labels act as the control commands to the Brick controller. These commands can be used to assist a motor disabled person to control different devices to meet his basic needs.

articleTitle: CAD System for Detection and Classification of Liver Cancer using Optimization Neural Network & Convolution Neural Network Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Deep learning is a recent field of machine learning that has garnered a great deal of attention in recent years. It has been commonly used for a variety of applications and has proved to be a strong machine learning method for many complex problems. Liver cancer appears to be a leading cause of female death, and a lot of money has been spent in the form of preventative screening programs. The use of automatic image processing techniques resulting from deep learning in that same sense represents a promising way of helping to detect liver cancer. In this paper, ADF-USM (Anisotropic diffusion filtering with Unsharp masking) completed the liver malignant growth CT (Computer Tomography) image preprocessing, the shapes and curves were effectively differentiated and upgraded by histogram equalization. It is seen by analyzing the results of the division method that the SSBIC (Superpixel Segmentation Based Iterative Clustering) algorithm produces favorable results than other current strategies. Finally, the process for classification relies mostly on execution of AGWO-CNN (Adaptive Grey Wolf Optimization with Convolution Neural Network classifier) to verify whether the images are benign or malignant.Experimental results on CT images show that the AGWOCNN model achieved high processing efficiency with an accuracy of 97.6 percent in the classification of liver cancer compared to other classification models.

Author Keywords: Anisotropic diffusion filtering with Unsharp masking
Adaptive Grey Wolf Optimization with Convolution Neural Network classifier

articleTitle: Utility Synchronization of PV-WGS-BES Based Distributed Generation Microgrid Using ITOF-FLL Control Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The dynamic performance of the conventional phaselocked loop (PLL) leads to frequency divergence and oscillations in the converter’s power output. Thus, this paper implements improved third-order filter (ITOF) frequency-locked loop as an efficient grid converter control and theta (θ) extraction method for utility synchronization (US). This manages the renewable energy sources (RES) based microgrid in both standalone and utility tied mode, while feeding loads with green and uninterrupted power. This control also provides a fast and accurate assessment of the harmonics component of load currents with their respective phases of synchronization to execute microgrid in its generic utility conditions. ITOF control is implemented with a frequency-locked loop (FLL), making the control frequency adaptive. Therefore, in comparison to the PLL approach, the implemented ITOF-FLL control has reduced complexity, faster, precise in frequency tracking and easier parameter tuning. This control algorithm eliminates harmonics of load current thereby reducing the total harmonic distortion (THD) of the PCC current. Accordingly reducing the THD within acceptable IEEE 519 limits. The behavior of the ITOF-FLL control under load and generation perturbation is validated by simulation results, which demonstrates its excellent performance.

articleTitle: Selection of Power Flow Algorithm for Closed Loop Volt-Var Control
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper focuses on closed loop operational mode of Volt-VAr control (VVC) algorithm, as well as the power flow (PF) methods that can successfully be used to implement VVC. Two methods to implement efficient PF are Newton-Raphson approach and current iteration approach. The paper compares both approaches to find the one most suitable for the implementation of closed loop VVC algorithm.

articleTitle: Solar Umbrella Using L3C Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper proposes a solar patio umbrella using L3C Resonant Converter. The patio umbrella can work as an outdoor workspace and at the same time produce electrical energy from sunlight incident on the solar panels mounted on the umbrella. A L3C resonant converter is used as dc-dc converter which converts the dc output of solar panel to the required value. A microcontroller is used to provide the switching frequency for the converter. To improve the irradiance over the solar panel, a single axis solar tracking system is used. The paper proposes a control algorithm for operation of the L3C resonant converter and a modified perturb and observe algorithm for obtaining the maximum power from solar panel, both simulated in MATLAB Simulink. A prototype of single axis solar tracking system has been made and tested.

articleTitle: High Alpha Maneuvering with a Laterally Asymmetric Fighter Aircraft: A Backstepping Control Approach
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Asymmetric release of payload or partial damage of wing shifts the center-of-gravity (c.g.) of a fighter aircraft to new positions resulting in a highly coupled and nonlinear asymmetric dynamics. Since controlling the aircraft becomes much more challenging when it tries to perform some high alpha maneuver with such lateral asymmetry, implementation of nonlinear control becomes mandatory for the safety of the aircraft. In the present paper, the highly coupled asymmetric dynamics is first converted to the strict feedback form and thereafter a backstepping control is designed to autonomously execute the high alpha cobra maneuver under significant lateral c.g. shift. The simulation results show the maneuver performance under lateral asymmetry to be almost the same as that without any asymmetry.

articleTitle: A Survey On Recent Approaches In Image Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Image reconstruction is an ongoing research in medical image processing. It is a continuously developing field. The aim is to reconstruct the images from some noise or something else without loss of image quality and accuracy of the reconstructed images. Medical image processing is one of the most trending research area. Medical images are widely used in various applications like medical segmentation, Brain tumor detection, early prediction of Alzheimer's Disease and its variations, etc. The types of medical images are Magnetic Resonance Images(MRI), Positron Emission Tomography(PET), X-Ray images, computerized tomography (CT), single-photon emission CT(SPECT etc. There is a high radiation dose that occurs when taking these types of images for the disease diagnosis and is costly. Also, there exist some limitations in the number of images. This is why we need image reconstruction. Here exact copy of the same images are reconstructed without any loss of image quality and spatial resolution.It also reduces the radiation dose. So image reconstruction is very important and these images can be used in various applications.

articleTitle: Speed Control in Serpentine Locomotion using Sliding Mode
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Speed control of a planar snake robot which is not wheeled is investigated in this paper. Sliding mode control is used to devise robust control for speed which is the first of its kind for wheel-less planar snake robots. The robustness is verified in MATLAB simulation and compared with PI control employed in one of the literature for speed control. The tracking results show that employment of sliding mode control is more effective and it outperforms the existing control schemes for speed control of wheel-less serpentine robots. To further validate the effectiveness, a disturbance signal is given and the results depict improved performance in case of sliding mode control.

articleTitle: Multifunctional Control of Weak Grid Intertie Solar PV System with Synchronization Capability
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The multifunctional operation of an adaptive digital filter along with synchronization capability is presented in this paper. The performance is validated during reduction of solar insolation, load unbalancing and grid outage mode. When the grid is present, power transfer occurs from the solar PV array to the utility grid and local loads connected at the point of common coupling (PCC) along with distribution static compensator (DSTATCOM) capabilities. The total harmonic distortion (THD) of the grid current is in compliance with an IEEE-519 standard thereby guaranteeing satisfactory performance along-with reduction in losses of the distribution network. Moreover, during grid outage or islanded mode of operation, the voltage controller is utilized for delivering power from solar PV array to local loads. The performance is validated though simulation results and the system behaviour is observed for unbalanced load, variable solar insolation and grid connected-islanded mode change conditions.

articleTitle: PWM-Based Sliding Mode Current Controller for Bidirectional DC-DC Converters in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: In this paper, design and analysis of sliding mode current controller (SMCC) applied to bidirectional DC-DC converter in Electric vehicles (EVs) is presented. The enhancement in control architectures will greatly contribute to electric vehicle technology. A pulse width modulation (PWM) based SMCC is described for both buck and boost operation of the bidirectional DC-DC converter. SMCC maintains stability and give consistent performance to bidirectional DC-DC converter and the results are validated using Typhoon Virtual hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) environment.

articleTitle: Modeling the Effect of Additives on Metal Oxide Chemiresistor Gas Sensors
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The additives change the conductance of the metal oxide chemiresistor gas sensor. A model based on the Freundlich adsorption isotherm, giving a power law relation between the electrical conductance of the gas sensor and the concentration of the target gas, describes the steady state response of the metal oxide chemiresistor gas sensor in the best manner. In this paper, the effect of platinum (Pt) and palladium (Pd) on various tin dioxide (SnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) nanostructures are analyzed and the model parameters are evaluated for the conduction model based on adsorption. The model parameters are fitted using the data extracted from different papers that report the effect of additives to tin dioxide (SnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) in sensing gases like hydrogen (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>), carbon monoxide (CO), nitric oxide (NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>), or ethanol (C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>OH). The model parameters are evaluated for the sensing material with and without the additives. The result shows that not only the exponent but also the pre-exponential coefficient, of the power law relation, is changed when doping is done to the sensing material. The major amount of conductance change is observed to be due to the power law exponent when SnO2 with Pt is used for detecting gases like CO, NO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, and H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, etc., while the pre-exponential factor controls conductance change when SnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> with Pd is used in detecting H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. Even though this study is done on SnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> with palladium or platinum, it can be shown that the steady state response of most of the metal oxide chemiresistors with additives can be modeled by the method proposed.

articleTitle: Hybrid Fractal Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Every communication system inevitably needs an antenna for transmission and reception of signals. A modern-day wireless communication system put various demands on the antenna such as multi-band working, compact structures and low cost. Fractal geometry comprises of a self-repeating pattern that ends in infinitely intricate fine structures. Fractal geometries increase the electrical length of the antenna, without increasing the physical dimension. Therefore, it makes a suitable option for miniaturisation and multiband applications.This project presents a hybrid fractal antenna. Hybrid geometry brings out the best of both the parent geometries. The hybrid geometry is created out of Sierpinski carpet and Giuseppe Peano fractal geometries. The Sierpinski carpet is modified using Giuseppe Peano at the edges. The antenna is designed using OpenEMS software version 5.1.0. The antenna is designed on FR-4 substrate. It is found that the number of operational frequencies has increased from 8 GHz to 9 GHz and there is an operational bandwidth enhancement of approximately 400 MHz in the higher frequencies between 9 10 GHz. Apart from that, the highest gain of the antenna has increased from 6.003 dB to 9.582 dB, the antenna efficiency from 25.05% to 30.14% and the directivity from 6.634 dB to 9.5825 dB. These results indicate that the use of hybrid fractal greatly reduces the size of the antenna, effectively miniaturising it. The proposed structure is expected to work for wireless applications.

articleTitle: Improved Performance of a Bank-to-turn Missile Using Quantitative Feedback Theory Based Robust Controller
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: In this paper, a quantitative feedback theory based robust controller is proposed to improve the performance of a bank-to-turn (BTT) missile. The proposed controller provides reduced sensitivity with respect to parametric uncertainty, robust stability as well as robust tracking. A two-degrees-of-freedom (2-DOF) control structure consisting of a feedback controller and a pre-filter is used. The controller provides the required sensitivity, stability and partial tracking. The pre-filter is designed to meet the tracking specifications explicitly. Lastly, effectiveness of the controller is validated by computing the error speculation of achievable criteria.

articleTitle: Quadtree Compression Based Method for High Capacity Reversible Data Hiding in Encrypted JPEG Images
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The existing methods of reversible data hiding in encrypted JPEG images vacates space for data hiding after encrypting the image. This results in information loss as entropy in encrypted images is more. The complexity of image reconstruction is higher in such cases. The proposed method therefore finds space for data hiding before image encryption using the method of quadtree compression. Then the image is encrypted using RC4 encryption algorithm. The secret data bits are embedded into the MSB bit of pixels obtained after quadtree compression with the help of data hiding key. The data extraction and image recovery is made separable at the receiver side such that the secret data can be extracted without knowing the image contents. Original pixel restoration is done using prediction error method. The experimental results show that the proposed method is able to achieve better data hiding capacity and recovered image quality within an acceptable complexity range.

articleTitle: Power Quality problems And Mitigation Using D-STATCOM With H-bridge topology In Solar PV Integrated Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper presents Power Quality (PQ) problems and mitigation using D-STATCOM with H-Bridge topology in solar Photo Voltaic (PV) integrated distribution system. D-STATCOM solve current related issues of networks. Three-phase, four-wire, 400 V and 50 Hz system is selected as distribution source. The power quality improvement along with PV integration is intended by using D-STATCOM. Another goal is to design the components of shunt compensator for a PV integrated three phase distribution system. The Custom Power Device (CPD) is 50 kVA rated and uses battery storage system. Economical and robust design is ensured. Various loads were connected in the system for simulation studies and results were analyzed and validated.

articleTitle: Testing Impedance Based Fault Location Using Orthogonal Components For Different Fault Parameters
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Fault location is one of the most common aspects of power system analysis and protection. In order to maintain system's stability and avoid long lasting blackouts, it is important to localize a fault in shortest possible time. This paper analyzes already published impedance-based fault location methods and suggests new algorithm based on orthogonal components. Proposed method is applied on Simulink created three phase model, considering various system specifications including different fault resistance values, having more than one fault on a line at different locations, grounded and ungrounded generators effects, sampling rate changes, line length effects, etc. The results are indicating good accuracy of the algorithm itself.

articleTitle: PICC 2020 Plenary Speakers
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Provides an abstract for each of the plenary presentations and may include a brief professional biography of each presenter. The complete presentations were not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Load Flow Analysis of Islanded Droop Regulated Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Load flow studies are necessary for power system planning, analysis, operation, and optimization. A modified algorithm that can solve the load flow for the islanded radial microgrid is proposed in this paper. Droop controlled DGs are used in the microgrid rather than conventional DGs. Instead of using slack buses, one bus is selected as a reference and provides voltage reference and necessary power to the system. Frequency and voltage get updated to compensate for the active and reactive power. The convergence of the proposed load flow is tested and verified. The algorithm is based on the Backward/Forward Sweep method with modifications. Simulations are carried out in the MATLAB software and the proposed method is found to be accurate, simple, and easy to implement. The results with and without DGs for the 33 bus system is analyzed.

articleTitle: Word Boundary Estimation of isiZulu Continuous Speech
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Typical automatic speech recognition algorithms assume that spoken words are completely isolated; this is not always the case in real-world applications. Consequently, there is a need for intra-sentence segmentation of words uttered in a continuous speech. Word boundary estimation is a method that was proposed for the separating of words. There has been extensive research on western languages, especially English. However, limited investigations have been done for indigenous languages. IsiZulu is the most spoken indigenous language in South Africa. This paper proposes the use of prosodic features and higher-order statistic (HOS) features to classify IsiZulu speech segments i.e. noise, voice and boundary. For automatic classification, supervised learning was used.

articleTitle: Implementation of Reconfigurable Data Encryption Technique using different AES versions
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The Advanced Encryption Standard is widely used for encrypting data today. Unauthorized individuals will not be able to access data encrypted using AES. This paper presents the implementation of three different variants of AES in FPGA using Reconfiguration. The hardware utilization is a major factor considered to reduce the area used on a chip and thus the system cost. Using the reconfiguration feature of the FPGA, the different AES versions implemented can be loaded as and when required with reduced hardware utilization.

articleTitle: Exponentially Weighted Laguerre Function based Model Predictive Controller for a Twin Rotor MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Model Predictive Control (MPC) is a viable control scheme for constrained nonlinear MIMO systems but the high computational complexity and numerical sensitivity issues associated with long prediction horizons hamper the real-time implementation of this control technique. To alleviate the computational burden and problems associated with numerical ill-conditioning, an Exponentially Weighted Laguerre Function based Model Predictive Controller (EWLMPC) is proposed in this paper. EWLMPC deploys orthonormal Laguerre functions to parametrize the control input trajectory which helps in alleviating the real-time computational load. The inclusion of exponential data weight facilitates the use of large prediction horizons without jeopardizing the numerical stability of the algorithm. The effectiveness of the controller is established through experimental studies on a benchmark MIMO system, the Twin Rotor Multi-Input Multi-Output System (TRMS).

articleTitle: A Modified H-Bridge Transformerless PhotoVoltaic Neutral-point-clamped inverter with constant common mode voltage
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Nowadays, transformerless PV inverters (TPVI) are more popular due to its excellent features such as lower in size, cost and higher in efficiency, as compared with conventional inverters. Undoubtedly it leads dangerous leakage current via stray capacitors to the ground, which results higher current ripples and problems related to electromagnetic interference (EMI). Therefore, a several configurations have been proposed with reduced leakage current and constant common-mode voltage (CMV). In this paper a modified H-bridge structure is proposed with rectifier circuit at mid-point of the dc-link capacitor to keep constant CMV in the whole grid cycle namely M-HB topology. The theoretical findings of the M-HB inverter are tested through simulation results. At the end a fair comparative analysis is presented.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Mother Wavelet Functions and Thresholding Methods for Denoising EEG Signals during Cognitive Tasks
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Artifact reduction is a major challenging task in the analysis of Electroencephalography signals. Wavelet denoising is one of the efficient techniques for rejecting artifacts and it has been employed in the detection of various brain diseases. The selection of the most suitable wavelet function and the thresholding method, which varies with the nature of the task performed, are important steps in the process of wavelet denoising. In this study, the effects of wavelet denoising on Electroencephalograph (EEG) signals during reading and mental arithmetic tasks were investigated. The effectiveness of each of the 46 wavelet functions including Daubechies- db, Symlet- sym, Coiflet- coif and Discrete Meyer- dmey, was examined for denoising the EEG signals recorded during reading and mental arithmetic tasks. EEGs of ten healthy subjects were recorded during reading and mental arithmetic tasks. The performance evaluation of wavelet function and thresholding method were done on the basis of peak signal to noise ratio (PSNR), root mean square error (RMSE), percentage root square difference (PRD), and cross correlation coefficient (CC). Subsequently, the EEG signals were decomposed into different frequency bands, and variations in EEG band power were computed before and after denoising. The wavelet function "dmey" was found to be the most efficient wavelet function for denoising EEG signals during cognitive tasks. Rigrsure thresholding method was found to be the best thresholding method in this study. A significant difference in EEG rhythmic activity (P <; 0.05) was observed after denoising the EEG signal.

articleTitle: Demand Response and Energy Storage System Participation in North American Electricity Markets
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Demand response (DR) and energy storage systems (ESS) are important resources for Independent System Operators (ISOs) to reduce the peak demand and electricity price spikes, balance the intermittency of renewable energy resources (RES), and increase power system resiliency, efficiency and reliability. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the current frameworks and programs for DR and ESS to participate in some electricity markets in North America (US and Canada). The modalities of DR participation in each ISO are classified based on: (i) their mode of procurement, (ii) their participation time-frame (day-ahead or real-time) and operational domain (energy, ancillary services, or capacity), and (iii) the type of DR programs. Also, a comprehensive study of the ancillary services market structure, ESS procurement process, and deployment timeline is discussed.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Detection and Classification of Power System Events
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Rapid rise in energy demand has put a huge pressure on the electrical grid and presented major difficulties for device operators in providing stable and safe power supply. Real-time monitoring of power systems enables timely and effective post-event control actions. Phasor Measurement Units (PMU) may be used to obtain time-synchronized measurement data at very large reporting speeds, mitigating the SCADA technology drawback. This enables PMU to monitor the power system dynamically. The real-time Synchrophasor data is further processed to detect and classify the events in the power system whenever it arises. This paper presents a robust machine learning based event detection and classification technique using PMU data. Wavelet analysis is an important signal processing method for detecting events from PMU data with non-stationary characteristics. Machine learning algorithms are used to classify the observed power system events. Significant characteristics are extracted and the classifier is trained using the PMU samples. The features of the machine learning algorithms are optimized to minimize the classification errors. The proposed algorithm to detect and classify the events using wavelet analysis and machine learning algorithms is validated on a WSCC 9-bus system.

articleTitle: Mean Normalized Multi-objective Predictive Control for Matrix Converters with Common-mode Voltage Elimination
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper presents a method to realize multiple objectives of sinusoidal source and load currents in a direct matrix converter (DMC) fed system using finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) without any weighting factors in the cost function. Moreover, this is achieved while maintaining zero common-mode voltage (CMV) by utilizing only those switching states of the DMC that switch three different input phases at the load terminals in each switching state. Further, the input power factor is also maintained near unity. The absence of any proportionality factors corresponding to the errors in source and load currents in the cost function is the result of a scaling algorithm based on statistical mean normalization that automatically adjusts the errors to a directly comparable scale before implementing a switching state. Simulation and experimental results are presented in this paper validating the proposed method of control and comparing its performance with an optimum weighting factor based predictive current control scheme for a three-phase to three-phase DMC.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Strategy for DC-Link control of Active Front End for Four Quadrant Drives
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The conventional voltage-oriented control strategy for Active Front Ends (AFE) is being modified by using an adaptive outer loop control in this paper. The control strategy suggested aims to provide a constant and steady DC link voltage with minimal ripple to the load in both motoring as well as regenerating modes. The adaptive PI controller as name suggests has proportional and integral gains which adjust themselves depending upon the error between reference voltage and DC link voltage and attempts to achieve a better control in overall loading conditions. Furthermore, unity power factor operation along with better transient response, and grid current THD's within standard specified limits in all quadrants of operation are essential requirements for AFE's which help in testing the effectiveness of the strategy. Additionally, comparison of the technique with well-established technique like symmetrical optimum method is been provided in the paper. The simulation and experimental results conducted on 60 kW back to back converter system used for driving a load-controlled induction motor is being presented in this paper which validate the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Evolutionary Algorithms for a CSTR System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: A PID controller has three adjustable tuning parameters, i.e. proportional gain, integral gain and derivative gain; these three parameters are adjusted using three optimization algorithms: i.e. Particle Swarm Optimization, Ant Colony Optimization and Bees Algorithm. These algorithms are implemented to optimize a linearized model of Continuous Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) which is a nonlinear system. The results are compared on account of (1) Controller Tuning parameters (2) Performance Index (ISE) (3) Time Domain Specifications such as Settling Time, Peak Overshoot etc. This paper focuses on a novel approach for comparative study of these three algorithms and suggesting the best algorithm for nonlinear systems.

articleTitle: Control of Multifunctional PV-Battery Storage System with Power Quality Enhancement of Utility Grid
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper presents the control for the multifunctional photovoltaic (PV) battery storage system with power quality (PQ) enhancement of utility grid. The current control of voltage source converter (VSC) utilizes adjustable momentum factor with normalized error based filter in the grid intertied mode at normal operation and in the voltage control of VSC, when the utility grid disrupts as a result of some contingency at the distribution network. In this system, the assemblage of the battery is by using a DC-DC bidirectional converter, which is discharged and charged as per the load perturbations. It also maintains the voltage for maximum power point (MPP) tracking at the DC link. The control has smooth and fast convergence, as active weight current constituent of nonlinear load is obtained by adjustable momentum term with weight updates of preceding two values and variable step size with normalized error. The current control is utilized for power factor correction, harmonics eradication and enhancement of system’s dynamics with PV feed-forward part. The system’s behaviour is found satisfactory and validated through test results in steady state and dynamic scenarios i.e. solar insolation and load alteration, load unbalance, grid voltages anomalous condition, like swell / sag. The smooth transition operation via a solid state switch between two modes, ensures uninterrupted and suitable power to the load at the utility grid outage. The perturb and observe (P & O) technique is utilized to obtain MPP from PV array. The voltage control technique regulates load frequency and voltage during grid fault.

articleTitle: Voltage Stability Analysis Using Energy Function Considering the Transmission-Microgrid Coupling and Microgrid Operation in Islanded Mode
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The significant benefits associated with microgrids (MG) lead to their increasing insertion in electrical power systems. The presence of intermittent sources, load demand variations, and the possibility for the MG to operate connected or isolated from the main grid demand an assessment of the transmission-microgrid coupling. Thus, this paper proposes voltage stability analysis in transmission systems considering the transmission-microgrid interaction using an energy function. The methodology identifies if the system is close to the voltage collapse and identifies the best microgrids to have load shedding, alleviating the system's overall condition. The proposed methodologies are validated in a modified IEEE 37 node test feeder and IEEE 30 bus system.

articleTitle: Dual Mode Control of AC Microgrid to Facilitate Seamless Transition Between Operating Modes
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: The battery energy storage plays a key role in integrating the energy generated from renewable energy resources such as wind and solar photovoltaic (PV) into the grid. The share of battery becomes prominent for the areas, which are not associated with the strong AC distribution network. Here, in this work, wind and solar power based microgrid is interfaced to a 3 phase-4 wire (3P4W) AC distribution network with dual mode control. This dual mode control consists of seamless transition between the grid to standalone/standalone to the grid operating mode. The battery resiliency generates additional revenue by ensuring the operation during grid outage mode by reducing the downtime expense. In the case of grid failure, the control seamlessly transits from the current control to the voltage control. The grid connected mode and standalone mode of operation are enabled according to the signal provided to the static transfer switches (STS). The system control eradicates the intermittency issues raised by the renewable resources. The battery along with the mode transition control, provides an improvement in the power quality (PQ) while ensuring the power supply reliability and surety in feeding the local loads. The square root normalized least mean square (SR-NLMS) adaptive filter is used to extract the fundamental load current component in on-grid operating mode. The enhanced proportional resonant (PR) controller along with prefilter integrated second order generalized integrator based phase locked loop (PI-SOGI-PLL) is utilized for the voltage control mode. The system performance is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink environment and the co-operational behavior of the microgrid is observed for different practical conditions.

articleTitle: Application of Signal Processing in the Detection of Urinary Dysfunction: A Review on Different Techniques
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: Urinary dysfunction is a disorder that may occur due to the pathological conditions like spinal cord injury, neurological disorders or because of the non-pathological reasons like aging. There are several methods for the detection of urinary dysfunction. Urodynamics testing is the medical procedure for the detection of urinary dysfunction. It analyses conditions like, frequent urination, incontinence, infections and obstructions in urinary lower tract or bladder muscle hyperactivity. The urodynamic studies evaluate the pressure flow relationship between the bladder and urethra and give the functional information about lower urinary tract. It can be done either by some simple observations or by some precise measurements using sophisticated equipments. In this paper different methods for the detection of urinary dysfunction are explained. And it describes how signal processing can be applied to improve the result for better diagnosis.

articleTitle: Learning Rate Optimisation of an Image Processing Deep Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Power, Instrumentation, Control and Computing (PICC)
abstract: This paper proposes the use of a mathematical model to identify an optimal learning rate (OLR) for an image processing deep convolutional neural network (DCNN). An OLR may be realized by defining the relationship between the learning rate and model performance. This relationship is meant to resolve the problem of arbitrarily selecting the initial learning rate. The benefit of an OLR includes improved training stability and reduced computational resources. An algorithm is developed to analyze an inputted DCNN model and subsequently render output parameters that may be used to aid in the selection of an OLR. The results rendered by the OLR algorithm proposes that an optimal learning rate improves model performance. The mathematical model is also capable of approximating the model performance to a high degree of accuracy averaging at 91%. Furthermore, a model validation graph is also extrapolated, which will illustrate the mathematical model accuracy and the region of interest (ROI); the ROI defines a region in the learning rate spectrum with a positive effect on model performance.
